chunks: Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked: Why did the Maghrib prayer become three rak'ahs, with four after it, and why is there no shortening in it whether in residence or travel? So he said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down upon His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله every prayer as two rak'ahs. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله added to each prayer two rak'ahs in residence, and shortened them in travel, except Maghrib and the morning prayer. Then when he صلى الله عليه وآله prayed Maghrib, news of the birth of Fatimah عليها السلام reached him, so he added to it one rak'ah in gratitude to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then when al-Hasan عليه السلام was born, he added to it two rak'ahs in gratitude to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then when al-Husayn عليه السلام was born, he added to it two rak'ahs in gratitude to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then he said:
For the male is the like of the share of two females.
So he left it in its state in residence and travel.

key_terms.الْمَغْرِبُ: the Maghrib prayer, the sunset salat
key_terms.شُكْرًا: an act of gratitude to Allah

ai.seo_question: Why is the Maghrib prayer not shortened during travel in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains why Maghrib remains three rak'ahs and is not shortened in travel, unlike other prayers. It links the form of the prayer to the Prophet's صلى الله عليه وآله additions and to acts of gratitude connected with the births of Fāṭimah, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn عليهم السلام, while also invoking a Qur'anic expression about proportional share.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1317 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked:
"Why is the Maghrib prayer three rak'ahs with an additional four rak'ahs (supererogatory) afterward, and why is there no shortening of it during residence or travel?"
Imam (as) said:

"Indeed, Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, revealed to His Prophet (sw) every prayer as two rak'ahs. The Messenger of Allah (sw) added two rak'ahs to each prayer in residence and shortened them during travel, except for the Maghrib and Fajr (morning) prayers. When the Prophet (sw) performed the Maghrib prayer, he was informed of the birth of Sayyida Fatimah Al-Zahra {S.A}, so he added a rak'ah out of gratitude to Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic. When Hasan (as) was born, he added two more rak'ahs out of gratitude to Allah (swt), and when Hussain (as) was born, he added two more rak'ahs out of gratitude to Allah (swt).
He then said: 'For a male, the share is twice that of a female,'
and thus he left the prayer in its current form during residence and travel."
